claims.text: Atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity in CoCrFeNi nanopillars creates spatial variations in generalized stacking-fault energy.
Spatial stacking-fault-energy variations promote coordinated activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip under tensile loading.
The coordination of twinning and dislocation slip delocalizes deformation and delays necking.
Delayed necking from coordinated twinning and slip produces an exceptional combination of tensile strength and ductility.
Rapid annealing retains pronounced local chemical heterogeneity in CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
Prolonged homogenization minimizes atomic-scale compositional fluctuations in CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
Post-processing heat treatments can tune atomic-scale compositional inhomogeneity and the associated stacking-fault-energy landscape.
Advanced TEM or atom-probe tomography can directly assess local stacking-fault-energy variations.
The proposed mechanism operates during room-temperature tensile deformation of single-crystalline CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
Lower-stacking-fault-energy regions preferentially activate deformation twinning.
Higher-stacking-fault-energy regions preferentially support dislocation slip.
Chemically heterogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillars will have a higher deformation-twin density than homogenized CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
Chemically heterogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillars will retain robust dislocation activity relative to homogenized nanopillars.
Chemically heterogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillars can approach approximately 110% tensile elongation while sustaining high flow stress.
Homogenized CoCrFeNi nanopillars will exhibit reduced ductility and a more conventional deformation response.
The hypothesis is bounded to CoCrFeNi nanopillars under room-temperature tensile deformation and may not transfer to substantially different length scales, temperatures, or alloy systems.
Simultaneous in situ TEM or atom-probe tomography can monitor local stacking-fault-energy evolution, twin formation, and dislocation structures during tensile loading.
